key_insight: The paper introduces a sound probabilistic verification framework for AI agent policies that upper-bounds violation risk even when probabilistic predicates may be correlated.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical runtime security monitoring for AI agents in uncertain environments, improving the security-utility trade-off without relying on unrealistic independence assumptions.
method: Formulate policy verification for probabilistic Datalog-style rules as a distributionally robust optimization problem.
Compute sound upper bounds on policy-violation probability under arbitrary correlations between probabilistic predicates.
Target runtime monitoring for security policies involving uncertain components such as PII detectors or declassifiers.
evidence_signal: On standard benchmarks for terminal and tool-calling agents, the method outperforms prior art while providing rigorous bounds on policy-violation probability.
watch_item: Soundness depends on the conservativeness of the bound, so tighter guarantees may come with some loss in utility or extra runtime cost.
paper_title: Efficient and Sound Probabilistic Verification for AI Agents
